svg.title: Three stacked tiers. The view is TypeScript always, rendering and capturing raw input, and owning picking, hit-testing and the camera locally. Below it the presenter owns interaction logic, and its runtime is a per-surface choice between TypeScript in-process and a WebAssembly build of the Go presenter. Below that the core is Go always, holding the IR, diff, rules and simulation. Between the view and the presenter, intents travel up and commands travel down over a duplex, typed contract.

g.text: renders, captures raw input, owns the GPU buffers and the DOM
picking, hit-testing and the camera are view-local, and it holds no domain logic

svg.text: the presenter, whose runtime is a per-surface choice

g.text: TypeScript in-process for a high-frequency surface, such as continuous dragging
a WebAssembly build of the Go presenter for a read-mostly one
IR, diff, rules and simulation: runtime-agnostic and authoritative
the same packages the CLI and the Go tests run headless

svg.text: the contract is typed interfaces in both directions, not an event bus and not a shared store
